ControlAuthority._comment: Who may command an asset, and what this deployment is attached to. AllowLiveControl is a GUARD, not a feature toggle: this build contains no hardware bearer - no serial link, no radio, no vehicle-side endpoint - so every command it accepts is executed by the in-process simulation and can move nothing real. Setting it true is therefore refused at startup rather than logged and ignored, because the failure being designed against is an operator who set it, watched the server come up, and concluded the console in front of them was driving a vehicle. It exists now so that the day a live path is added it arrives behind a gate that already defaults closed. GET /api/v2/sim/control/mode publishes the resolved mode so an interface can state it rather than assume it. MaxLeaseSeconds caps how long one control lease may run before it must be renewed - the bound that stops a browser tab which closed at the wrong moment from stranding a vehicle - and a longer request is granted at the cap rather than refused, so a client must read the granted duration back. AuditCapacity is how many lease records one session retains.

LocalOrigin._comment: Anchors the scene frame to the globe: the WGS84 point that local (0,0,0) sits on. Without it the server refuses geodetic command targets with configuration.localOriginMissing and withholds the Geo target shape from every capability report. This default is a placeholder chosen to match the alpine terrain the scene renders, not a description of any real deployment - override OriginId and the coordinates per site. Local positions are only comparable across scenes sharing an OriginId, so change the id whenever the coordinates change. YawRad turns local +X away from true east, positive toward north.

mixed-ground._comment: Air and ground working the same hillside. An entry with no 'class' is an air multirotor, exactly as every preset above; 'class' names a VehicleClass and 'domain' is optional documentation that must agree with the class the server derives. 'headingDeg' is clockwise from true north. Staged on the west flank of the alpine preset's east peak, where the ground genuinely has grade: terrain runs 32-51 m here against a -3 m water surface, so nothing spawns afloat, and the rovers sit on 6.5, 23.8 and 6.7 degree slopes - inside every profile's climb and cross-slope limits, with the tracked rover close enough to its own to make the mobility assessment mean something. A ground entry's 'pos' Y is ignored: a rover's height is read off the terrain under its footprint.

ground-convoy._comment: Three rovers strung up one fall line under a single air overwatch, spaced so the grade under them climbs along the column: 6.0, 15.2 and 23.8 degrees. The order is deliberate - the wheeled platforms hold the gentle ground and the tracked platform, which has the steepest climb limit and the widest safe cross-slope, takes the steep end. Driving the column upslope is what exercises grade derating and the traversability probe; driving it across the slope is what exercises the rollover assessment.

coastal-search._comment: Maritime search on the 'coastal' terrain preset, which is the only preset whose water surface (+3.0 m) sits above the datum - SELECT THAT PRESET BEFORE RUNNING THIS SCENARIO. A preset places assets and never touches the environment, so run against the default 'alpine' terrain every vessel here is placed on a hillside and reports itself aground; it stays commandable, but the demo is meaningless. Staged in the channel west of the main island: the three vessels float in 5.5 m of water for 4.95 m of under-keel clearance against a 0.55 m draft and a 0.305 m advisory margin - comfortably clear, and every straight leg between them sweeps at least 5.2 m so a transit ordered from one to another is not refused for a shoal. The rovers are ashore on ground that is dry (14-17 m) and gentle (under 7 degrees), so both spawn drivable. A ground or surface entry's 'pos' Y is ignored: a rover's height is read off the terrain under its footprint and a vessel's is the water surface where it floats. External contacts are NOT spawned from a preset - a track is an observation, and POST /api/v2/sim/tracks is deliberately the only way one enters a session.

coastal-transit._comment: A column of three vessels running north up the same channel under one air overwatch, for the 'coastal' terrain preset (select it first, as above). Deliberately narrower than coastal-search: one domain plus an eye in the sky, spaced 70-80 m apart along a straight line that never shoals below 5.5 m, so ordering the column to transit exercises the guidance law and the route sweep rather than the shoreline refusal. Heading 0 is due north, and the lead is the northmost hull.

flood-response._comment: All three domains working one inundated valley, and the only mixed preset that runs on the DEFAULT 'alpine' terrain - no environment change is needed before it starts. Alpine's water surface is -3.0 m and the shelf immediately west of the lake stands 7-11 m above it, which is what puts a drivable supply road within 150 m of navigable water: the three rovers hold that road on 2.0, 3.3 and 6.0 degree ground, the two ferries work the flooded valley in 10.3 and 13.2 m of water for 9.8 and 12.7 m of under-keel clearance against a 0.55 m draft, and the mapping lane crosses it from north-west to south-east with 122-153 m of clearance over the bed. The alpine lake stands in for the inundated ground - the terrain carries no flood model, and a preset places assets and nothing else. A ground entry's 'pos' Y is ignored (a rover's height is read off the terrain under its footprint) and a surface entry's is the water surface it floats on. 'headingDeg' is clockwise from true north; the supply column faces 180 (south, down the shore road) and the ferries face 270 (west, back towards the landing).

port-incident._comment: A waterfront incident on the 'coastal' terrain preset - SELECT THAT PRESET BEFORE RUNNING THIS SCENARIO. A preset places assets and never touches the environment, so on the default alpine terrain every hull here is on a hillside; it stays commandable, but the demo is meaningless. Staged on the east coast rather than the western channel coastal-search and coastal-transit use: the shoreline runs roughly north-south at x=640, the cordon holds dry ground 2-7 m above the water line at x=550 on 5.2-7.0 degree slopes, and the samplers work 5.5 m of water east of it for 4.95 m of under-keel clearance against a 0.55 m draft. That siting is deliberate. The current sets to the south-east at about 0.45 m/s, so an unpowered hull here has 2.5-3.0 km of open water downstream of it, where a berth in the western channel would leave it 55-105 m. RESTRICTED ZONES AND EXTERNAL CONTACTS ARE NOT PRESET DATA IN THIS BUILD: the environment sampler is wired to EmptyZoneSource, so nothing in configuration declares an EnvironmentZone, and a contact is an observation that only enters a session through POST /api/v2/sim/tracks. To complete the picture, report an inbound contact around (900, 150) and an outbound one around (1000, 400) - both in open water on the samplers' side of the shoreline - and remember a track carries no capabilities and no command endpoint.

link-loss-divergence._comment: One asset per domain, 200 m apart on a single east-west line, so the three link-loss policies read side by side in one view. NOTHING HERE SIMULATES A LINK DROP: LinkLossBehavior is a policy each asset declares and republishes in its domain state every frame, and the point of this preset is that the three declarations differ and can be read together - the multirotor returns to base, the rover stops and holds indefinitely at no power cost, and the vessel, which declares no StationKeep capability because a single-screw hull loses steerage below its minimum speed, drifts and alerts. PositionUncertaintyGrowthMps diverges with them, and that is the number an advisory search radius would be drawn from: effectively zero for the stopped rover, wind-bounded for the drone, and the full drift rate for the hull. The positions are what make the divergence honest rather than merely stated. The rover sits on 4.0 degree ground 4.8 m above the water line, so 'stop and stay put' is a real option and it can still drive off under its own power. The vessel sits in 7.1 m of water at the north-west end of the alpine lake, where the current sets 134 degrees true at 0.49 m/s and 1050 m - about 36 minutes - of water deeper than 1 m lies downstream, so the drift is long enough to watch and does not strand the hull in the first minute. Runs on the DEFAULT 'alpine' terrain.

mixed-load-150._comment: 150 assets - 50 air, 50 ground, 50 surface - on the DEFAULT 'alpine' terrain, for the load gate. Deliberately a plain lattice rather than a staged scene: the gate measures what the frame builder, the snapshot differ and the client do with a full session, and a layout with a story in it only adds ways for that measurement to be about the staging. Each domain gets one regular grid over ground that suits it, chosen so every cell is valid with no exceptions to carry - 50 hulls on a 30x60 m grid over the deep centre of the lake, where the shallowest cell still has 8.4 m of water; 50 rovers on a 30x25 m grid on the southern shelf, where the steepest cell is 8.1 degrees and the lowest stands 8.6 m above the water line; and 50 multirotors on a 30x60 m grid at 120 m, offset half a cell from the hulls so none sits directly above one, over a footprint where the tightest clearance over the bed is still 119 m. The counts are the session caps this build enforces: 50 is the per-session air limit and 150 is inside the 200-asset limit, so the same population is reachable one asset at a time through POST /api/v2/sim/assets. The rover classes cycle so all three ground motion models carry a third of the load rather than one carrying all of it.
